title: Power outage
label: UTILITIES
deck: Protect people, preserve essentials, and avoid the hidden hazards of a blackout.
tldr: Check the utility and local alerts, then deal with immediate medical, temperature, and water needs. Use battery light and conserve phone power. Run generators and other fuel-burning equipment outdoors, away from windows and vents; never use an oven or grill to heat a home.
steps: Find the outage map and local emergency alerts. If someone depends on powered medical equipment, use the backup plan and seek urgent help if that equipment cannot run.
Use flashlights rather than candles. Keep refrigerators and freezers closed. Unplug sensitive electronics if power is unstable, and leave one light on to show when service returns.
A generator, camp stove, grill, or vehicle can produce deadly carbon monoxide. Keep fuel-burning equipment outside and well away from openings; use a battery-powered CO alarm if available.
Contact neighbors who may need help. Conserve phone power, use text when calls are congested, and monitor official updates.
next: If the outage continues, plan for safe temperature, water, medication refrigeration, and a place to relocate if the home becomes unsafe. Check current food-safety advice before eating perishables after a prolonged outage.
watch: Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, or confusion near fuel-burning equipment can signal carbon monoxide exposure. Get into fresh air and call emergency services. Never enter a flooded area to operate electrical equipment.
